prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING INC" (ticker ADP), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "ADP", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Automatic Data Processing, Inc.
result.industry: Payroll, HR software and outsourcing (human capital management)
markets: Payroll processing and payroll tax filing
Benefits administration and retirement plan services

mission.plain: ADP aims to make work easier and fairer for people by running payroll and HR reliably for employers around the world.

about.plain: ADP makes sure people get paid the right amount, on time. Companies hand ADP the job of running their paychecks, taking out taxes and sending those taxes to the government. It also sells software for hiring, tracking work hours and managing health benefits. For many small businesses it can even act as the official co-employer that handles all HR paperwork.
about.customers: More than 1.1 million employers of every size, from small shops to global corporations, in over 140 countries.
about.everyday: Many people see the ADP logo on their pay stub, and the monthly ADP National Employment Report on U.S. private-sector jobs is widely reported in the news.

money.part: Payroll and HR software and services
money.plain: Payroll, tax filing, HR, time and benefits tools (RUN, Workforce Now, Lyric HCM)
Acting as co-employer for ~775,000 worksite employees, incl. benefits and insurance

money.part: Interest earned on client payroll money
money.plain: Interest on about $40 billion of client funds held before paydays
ADP Assist and AI agents built into payroll and HR products
New flexible HR and payroll platform for larger and global employers

result.summary: Yes. ADP has a durable advantage built on very high switching costs (client revenue retention of 92.1% in FY2026), the scale of paying workers for more than 1.1 million clients in 140+ countries, and decades of hard-to-copy tax and compliance know-how. Its moat is wide in payroll, though it is under pressure from modern cloud and AI-native rivals such as Rippling, Deel and Workday, and its growth is tied to employment levels.

pricingPower.evidence: FY2026 revenue rose 7% to $21,947.4M while Employer Services retention held at 92.1% and U.S. pays per control grew only 1%, so growth came largely from new bookings ($2.2B, +6%), price and product mix; gross margin rose from 42.4% in FY2021 to 46.4% in FY2026, but intense competition in small-business payroll limits aggressive price rises.

moats.evidence: Founded in 1949, ADP is the best-known payroll brand in the U.S., named to Fortune's Most Admired Companies list for the 20th straight year in 2026, and its National Employment Report gives it unusual public visibility.
Payroll is mission-critical and tied to tax filings, benefits and time systems, so clients rarely move: Employer Services client revenue retention was 92.1% in FY2026 (92.2% in FY2023).
Payroll data from over 1.1 million clients improves ADP's benchmarking and compliance tools, but one client's use does not directly make the product more valuable to another.

With $21.9B of FY2026 revenue and about $40.4B of average client funds earning $1,354.8M of interest, ADP spreads compliance, R&D ($1,028.8M) and service costs over a far larger base than most rivals.
Full-service multi-country payroll and large PEOs are concentrated among a few providers (ADP, Paychex, Insperity, TriNet), though the small-business and software segments are crowded.
ADP is the incumbent; newer cloud-native rivals such as Rippling and Deel are counter-positioning against it rather than the reverse.

Decades of handling payroll tax rules across U.S. states, localities and 140+ countries, plus reliable money movement at huge volume, are operational know-how that is slow and risky for newcomers to replicate.

Its anonymised payroll dataset is unique enough to power the ADP National Employment Report and a research partnership with the Stanford Digital Economy Lab, though it is not a hard barrier to competitors.

customers.evidence: Employer Services client revenue retention was 92.1% in FY2026, held near record levels for years (92.2% in FY2023), and ADP TotalSource was named Best PEO by Forbes Advisor in 2025; small-business review sites, however, often rate newer tools like Gusto and Rippling higher for ease of use.

talent.evidence: ADP has about 64,000 associates and appears on Forbes World's Best Employers (2025), America's Best Large Employers (2024, 2026), TIME World's Best Companies (2024-2025) and Fortune Most Admired (20 straight years to 2026), though it is not a top-tier destination for elite software engineers.

product.evidence: NelsonHall has rated ADP a leader in payroll services for 11 years and Fortune listed it among America's Most Innovative Companies 2024-2026; Lyric HCM live clients rose 94% in FY2026 Q4 and AI agents reach nearly all 1.1M clients, but in enterprise HCM Workday is often seen as the stronger suite and in SMB Rippling and Gusto win on user experience.

competitors.name: Paychex

competitors.name: Workday
competitors.note: Enterprise cloud HCM and payroll for large employers

competitors.name: UKG
competitors.note: Private HCM, payroll and workforce management for mid-market and enterprise

competitors.name: Dayforce
competitors.note: Mid-market/enterprise HCM and payroll; taken private by Thoma Bravo in February 2026

competitors.name: Paycom Software
competitors.note: Single-database payroll and HCM software for mid-sized companies

competitors.name: Paylocity
competitors.note: Cloud payroll and HCM for small and mid-sized businesses

competitors.name: Rippling
competitors.note: Private, fast-growing all-in-one HR, payroll, IT and global PEO/EOR platform

competitors.name: TriNet
competitors.note: PEO for small and mid-sized businesses, competing with ADP TotalSource

competitors.name: Insperity
competitors.note: PEO and HR outsourcing for small and mid-sized businesses

competitors.name: Deel
competitors.note: Private global payroll and employer-of-record services, competing in multi-country payroll

competitors.name: Intuit (QuickBooks Payroll)
competitors.note: Micro and small-business payroll bundled with QuickBooks

competitors.name: Justworks
competitors.note: Private PEO and payroll for small businesses

threats: AI-native and cloud-native HR platforms (Rippling, Deel, Workday agents) eroding ADP's position, the main reason the stock fell to about $188 in early 2026
Slower hiring or AI-driven workforce reductions: revenue scales with client headcount, and U.S. pays per control grew only 1% in FY2026
Falling interest rates would cut the $1.35B of FY2026 interest earned on client funds, which carries almost pure margin
Up-market moves by Paychex (Paycor acquisition) and private-equity-backed UKG and Dayforce intensifying mid-market competition
Rising health-insurance costs and worksite-employee growth of only about 2% in the PEO business
Security or service failures in moving more than $40B of client money would damage trust

ceo.name: Maria Black
ceo.background: Career ADP executive who joined in 1996 as a sales associate; led ADP TotalSource, Small Business Solutions and HR Outsourcing, and Worldwide Sales and Marketing, then President from 2022

c1.evidence: ADP leads payroll and HR outsourcing, but that is a mature industry: revenue grew 6.7% in FY2026 and FY2027 guidance is 5%-6%.

c2.evidence: Employers choose ADP for trusted, accurate payroll and tax compliance in 140+ countries plus breadth from small-business RUN to TotalSource PEO, and the resulting 92.1% revenue retention shows the advantage is hard to dislodge.

c3.evidence: Many workers know ADP from their pay stubs and the ADP jobs report, and it is the default name in U.S. payroll, but it is not a beloved consumer brand and SMB users often praise rivals like Gusto more.

c4.evidence: CEO Maria Black talks of making work 'easy, smart, and human' and 'designing a better world at work', but the messaging is corporate rather than a galvanising mission, and the company is run with a clear focus on steady EPS growth and dividends.

c6.evidence: “reliable, payroll, big, corporate, old-school”: the impression is mostly positive about trustworthiness, with some criticism of clunky interfaces and pushy sales.

c7.evidence: HR outsourcing and cloud HCM are large and growing markets, but ADP's growth of about 7% a year shows it rides employment and outsourcing trends rather than a fast secular wave like AI.

c8.evidence: ADP can push further into global payroll (Lyric HCM), workforce management (the acquired Workforce Software, now Workforce Suite) and AI agents, but these are adjacent markets rather than large new ones.

m1.evidence: Maria Black argues AI will reshape work 'at the task level rather than eliminating jobs at scale' and has rolled out ADP Assist and HCM agents, a credible but evolutionary vision.

m2.evidence: She is not a founder but a 30-year ADP veteran (joined 1996) who manages for the long term within a conservative corporate culture.

m4.evidence: ADP emphasises 'always designing for people' and premium client service, reflected in 92.1% retention and employer awards, though there is little public evidence of a distinctive servant-leadership style.

m5.evidence: ADP has kept launching new platforms (Lyric HCM, ADP Assist, HCM agents) and is on Fortune's America's Most Innovative Companies list 2024-2026, but its culture is known more for sales discipline than invention.

m6.evidence: Maria Black came up through sales and business-unit leadership, not engineering or product.

m7.evidence: No controversies attach to her, and ADP highlights inclusion awards and workforce research, but there is no evidence of a mission much bigger than running a well-managed business.

m7b.evidence: No record found of Maria Black giving a commencement speech at a top university.

m8b.evidence: She has a low-key, conventional executive profile rather than a famous public persona.

m9.evidence: Since she became CEO in 2023, revenue grew from $18.0B (FY2023) to $21.9B (FY2026), diluted EPS from $8.21 to $10.94, and ADP beat consensus EPS in each of the last eight quarters.

m10.evidence: ADP is cost-disciplined, guiding to 70-90 bps of FY2027 margin expansion with roughly flat headcount, but it is not known for Bezos-style frugality.

c10.evidence: ADP helps pay tens of millions of workers accurately and on time for over 1.1 million employers, an important but invisible service rather than a life-changing product.

p2.evidence: Paying workers correctly across thousands of tax jurisdictions and 140+ countries at huge scale is difficult and essential, but many rivals do it too.

f1.evidence: Revenue rose every year from $15,005.4M in FY2021 to $21,947.4M in FY2026 (about 7.9% a year).

f2.evidence: Gross margin rose from 42.4% (FY2021) to 46.4% (FY2026) and operating margin (revenue less costs of revenues and SG&A) from 22.2% to 26.3%.

f3.evidence: At June 30, 2026 debt was $5.1B against $4.23B of corporate cash and $5.44B of FY2026 operating cash flow, with $6.03B of positive equity (client fund balances excluded).

f4.evidence: Operating income rose from $3,324.6M (FY2021) to $5,779.0M (FY2026) and operating cash flow from $3,093.3M to $5,441.2M.

v1.evidence: ADP is the safe, full-service choice that can handle almost any payroll anywhere, but it is not clearly the best product: Workday leads enterprise HCM suites and Gusto and Rippling often win on ease of use.

v2.evidence: ADP was on Forbes World's Best Employers (2025), America's Best Large Employers (2024, 2026), TIME World's Best Companies (2024-2025) and Fortune's Most Admired Companies for the 20th straight year in 2026.

c5.evidence: If ADP vanished, over 1.1 million employers and their workers would face missed paychecks and tax filings until they switched, but competitors could take over within months.
